履修条件
The class will be taught live, also using Moodle as a form of uploading lecture materials (video, slide, etc.). It is a required class for International Course Master's students in the Graduate School of Integrated Science for Global Society, as well as for Doctoral students who received their Master's at a different institution. It is taught solely in English.
授業概要
研究者としての社会的使命あるいは研究者倫理、また「資源・環境」「生命・生存」「寛容・共生」「時空間多様性」など各コースの教育目標に関わる原理的なkeywordをテーマとして、講義をすすめる。コースを越えた複数教員によるリレー形式とするが、併せて統合的基礎力・俯瞰的視野の獲得を検証する場をもうける。地球社会統合科学府の国際コースの大学院生の必須授業である。
 This course is done in an ‘omnibus form’, consisting of fourteen classes: guidance, twelve lectures, and ‘essay presentation and discussion’.
 Six lectures are provided by instructors who belong to the different discipline units (courses) of the graduate school: ‘comprehensive earth sciences,’ ‘comprehensive science of biological environment,’ ‘international cooperation, security and safety,’ ‘social diversity and co-existence,’ ‘language, media and communication,’ and ‘comprehensive east Asian and Japanese studies’.
 The last class is ‘essay presentation’.
 Students are required to write an essay about a designated topic such as; ‘what do you think about ‘integrative interdisciplinarity’ from the perspective of global society? How can it be applied to your own research?’
 We will have discussion over such a topic, with reference to the presented essays.

全体の教育目標
地球史的・生物進化史・人類史的な長い時間軸の視点から、人類が直面している諸問題を的確に把握し、解決策を構想するための基礎力の育成をめざす。
The goal of this course is to deepen the students’ understanding of “integrative interdisciplinarity”, which is a main principle of the Graduate School of Integrated Sciences for Global Society. This series of lectures is designed to help students understand various kinds of social issues, and pursue solutions to these issues at an introductory level. Lectures will be proceeded by the faculty of various discipline in the graduate school, with reference to several important concepts of GSIS such as “environment & resources”, “life and existence”, and “tolerance and coexistence”.
